radar.comment: Begin radar at its lowercase header, allowing its joined or separate colon. radar.md#detection: Accepted headers are radar-beta, radar-beta: and radar-beta followed by a separate colon. radar.md#names-and-keyword-boundaries: The joined radar-beta: form has no additional boundary: it can touch axis, title or hidden-yaml. common.md#leading-whitespace: Whitespace, line terminators, directives, and comment regions before the first unit of the diagram's lexer are trivia and are not seen by the diagram's grammar.

patterns.comment: Reuse hidden YAML and its shared line-based approximation. radar.md#hidden-forms-and-comments: After ASCII padding, hidden-yaml starts with ---, optional ASCII padding and LF. Try a body ending in LF before its closing --- first, taking as few body characters as permit that match; only if that fails try adjacent empty fences. Content can include LF, LS and PS. A closer starts immediately after a body LF, without indentation, and ends before LF, common Notation whitespace or EOF. A nonqualifying closer may be passed for a later qualifying one.

Reuse the native hidden directive form. radar.md#hidden-forms-and-comments: After optional ASCII padding, hidden-directive reads %%{ and arbitrary content, including LF/LS/PS or an empty/nonword body, through the earliest }%% ending before LF, common Notation whitespace or EOF. A nonqualifying closer can be passed.
Reuse native percent comments. radar.md#hidden-forms-and-comments: A native comment reads optional ASCII padding, %%, and maximal content before physical EOL.

Reuse the title and accessibility composites. radar.md#composite-common-forms: A title is title alone, or title followed by exactly one ASCII space/tab and a line value. Remaining padding belongs to the value. An accessibility title is accTitle, optional ASCII padding, colon and a line value. radar.md#composite-common-forms: A description line is the same form with accDescr. radar.md#composite-common-forms: A description block is accDescr, optional common Notation whitespace, an opening brace, arbitrary characters through the first closing brace, and that closer.

Read word keywords before ids, leaving a longer id whole. radar.md#names-and-keyword-boundaries: A longer name such as axisX is an id rather than axis. radar.md#names-and-keyword-boundaries: The same longer-id rule applies to axis, curve and all five option keywords.

Read the listed graticule and boolean values before ids. radar.md#names-and-keyword-boundaries: Boolean and graticule values have no suffix boundary. radar.md#grammar: showLegend takes only the fixed lowercase boolean words true/false; ticks, max and min take number; graticule takes only the unquoted lowercase words circle/polygon.

Read unsigned decimal numbers before ids, checking the dot boundary through following directives. radar.md#numbers-and-strings: The number rule first tries one or more ASCII digits, a dot and one or more ASCII digits, with no dot immediately after that candidate. Otherwise it tries the single digit zero, or a nonzero digit and further digits, again with no immediately following dot for the nonzero form. Repetitions take as many digits as the remaining condition permits. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.mermaid

patterns.comment: Reuse matching quoted labels and backslash escapes. radar.md#numbers-and-strings: A string opens with a single or double quote and closes with the matching quote. It may be empty. Inside it, take characters other than that quote or backslash, including LF, LS and PS; a backslash instead takes the next character, which must not be LF, CR, LS or PS. An unclosed string rejects.

Read separators, label delimiters and entry-list braces; description braces are read by the common form. radar.md#grammar: Each declaration has one id and an optional bracketed string label; a missing label differs from an empty string. radar.md#grammar: A curve requires braces and nonempty entries. radar.md#grammar: Commas separate members in the written group; empty members and trailing commas reject. radar.md#grammar: A named entry's colon is optional and its presence stays in the written punctuation; lexical priority still applies.

Read declared axis and curve ids and named-entry references. radar.md#names-and-keyword-boundaries: An id starts with an ASCII letter, digit or underscore, continues with those characters or dash, and cannot end with dash.
patterns.name: variable.mermaid
